To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the privacy utility tradeoff is affected by constraints, 2) the privacy utility region given only the (useful) data is no larger (smaller) than that given full (sensitive) data, and 3) the privacy utility regions given only the sensitive and useful (full) data coincide if and only if the common information between these data is equal to the common information between sensitive and useful (useful and sensitive) data, respectively

the privacy utility tradeoff is a function of the common information between sensitive and useful information, and is affected by whether or not the release mechanism is given the full data or only a subset thereof.

the optimal privacy utility region given only sensitive data is no smaller than the region given useful data, which is no smaller than that given full data, and the latter is equal to that given useful data when the common information between sensitive and useful is equal to the useful data itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of constraints on data availability on the privacy utility tradeoff for data release mechanisms.

understanding the effect of constraints on data availability on the privacy utility tradeoff, with the aim of identifying conditions under which the optimal tradeoff region given full data is achievable with only a subset of the available data.
the fundamental question of how much the utility of a privacy preserving mechanism is affected by the availability of only a subset of the data.

, given only sensitive data, the privacy utility tradeoff can be no better than that given only useful data, which can be no better that that given full data if and only if the common information between sensitive and useful is equal to the sensitive information.
the optimal tradeoff region given sensitive data is no smaller than that given only useful data, but is no larger than that given full data.

the tradeoff region with respect to full data is no larger (and possibly smaller) than the tradeoff region for only useful data, which is in turn no larger (and again possibly smaller) than that with respect to only sensitive data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the common information is an upper bound on the rate distortion region for constrained data release.
the privacy utility tradeoff is affected by the amount of common information between the useful and sensitive data and by the amount of useful data that is available for release.
the optimal privacy utility region is determined by the common information between sensitive and useful, and the availability of sensitive or useful data does not change this region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the privacy utility tradeoff can be determined without access to sensitive data, provided that the common information between sensitive and useful variables is known.
privacy utility tradeoffs can be studied in the presence of constraints on the input data.
, in the presence of privacy constraints, the utility of the data is a key factor in determining the optimal tradeoff between privacy and utility.
